entities.summary:
François-Joachim de Pierre de Bernis, comte de Lyonnais was a French cardinal and diplomat.
Born on May 22, 1715, in Saint-Marcel-d'Ardèche, he went on to become the sixth member elected to occupy Seat 3 of the Académie française in 1744. As a prominent figure during the Enlightenment period, Bernis played a significant role in shaping French politics and society.

His autobiography, 'Histoire de ma vie', was penned by Giacomo Casanova, providing valuable insights into the life of this influential cardinal.

Bernis's diplomatic career spanned several continents, including his time as ambassador to the Holy Roman Empire. He was instrumental in negotiating treaties between France and various European nations.

In 1794, Bernis passed away on November 3rd, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be studied by historians today.

A lasting cultural footprint of Bernis can be seen in the numerous institutions and organizations he helped establish during his lifetime, including the Académie française.

The French Revolution's impact on European politics cannot be overstated, with Bernis being a key figure in the events leading up to this pivotal moment in history. His diplomatic efforts played a crucial role in shaping the course of European history.

Bernis's significance can also be seen in his contributions to the field of cardiology, where he was a pioneering researcher and physician.

As a leading diplomat during the 18th century, Bernis's legacy extends far beyond France, with his diplomatic career influencing international relations for centuries to come.
